investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-25T20:23–20:30Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node production cluster has zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every remote agent pod to remain Unschedulable for ~138–145 seconds before the eval timeout. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never started.
investigation.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 are eligible for kata peer-pod scheduling, and both report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm — meaning the allocatable VM slots on those nodes are fully consumed. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector, so they are never considered. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every new remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable and the eval probe times out before any VM is assigned, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) empty. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all allocatable VM slots, leaving none for new probe pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes also lack capacity, every new pod is immediately Unschedulable. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

QUATERNARY — the kata peer-pod provider quota or the underlying cloud VM quota for the node pool may have been reduced or hit an external limit, shrinking the number of available VM slots below what concurrent probes require.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-25T20:23–20:30Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node production cluster has zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), causing every remote agent pod to remain Unschedulable for ~138–145 seconds before the eval timeout. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never started.
investigations.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 are eligible for kata peer-pod scheduling, and both report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm — meaning the allocatable VM slots on those nodes are fully consumed. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector, so they are never considered. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every new remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable and the eval probe times out before any VM is assigned, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) empty. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all allocatable VM slots, leaving none for new probe pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes also lack capacity, every new pod is immediately Unschedulable. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

QUATERNARY — the kata peer-pod provider quota or the underlying cloud VM quota for the node pool may have been reduced or hit an external limit, shrinking the number of available VM slots below what concurrent probes require.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the VM slot resource is fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no allocatable capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector at all, meaning the schedulable pool is effectively limited to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their labels changed, the effective capacity would drop to zero even without VM exhaustion.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for the remote-agents VM pool: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent eval runs plus any live workloads sharing the same resource.
Lower confidence — transient burst of concurrent remote-agent workloads at the time of the eval run consuming all available VM slots simultaneously, causing a temporary but recoverable exhaustion.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A subsequent eval run where remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all pass would indicate the VM resource exhaustion was transient and has self-resolved.
kubectl describe nodes showing kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is non-zero and available on the affinity-matching nodes would disprove current exhaustion.

Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude previously eligible nodes would shift the primary cause from VM exhaustion to a misconfiguration, not resource exhaustion.

A passing run of the local-agent equivalents (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) at the same time would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote/kata VM pool and not a broader API or auth failure.
Scheduler logs showing the pod was eventually scheduled (even if slowly) would suggest a transient burst rather than sustained exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on remote-agent-eligible nodes and fails when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing earlier warning before full exhaustion.

Add an eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector is at or above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that measures time-to-scheduled for a remote-agent pod and warns when it exceeds a threshold well below the current 138–145s observed stuck duration, enabling earlier detection of capacity pressure.

Add a sibling-correlation eval rule: if remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all fail with Unschedulable in the same run, auto-escalate to a shared-dependency infrastructure alert rather than treating each as an independent check failure.
